title: Extension of Temporary Electricity Contracting Support Scheme
what_it_is: Extension of Temporary Electricity Contracting Support Scheme

sections.label: TRECS extension and retailer guidelines
sections.summary: EMA is asked whether it will extend TRECS beyond May 2022 and require retailers to offer it with guidelines.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether EMA will consider extending the Temporary Electricity Contracting Support Scheme (TRECS) beyond May 2022; (b) if so, whether EMA will (i) require all electricity retailers to offer TRECS to consumers and (ii) consider providing guidelines to electricity retailers for TRECS to avoid unfair contractual terms and encourage greater take-up rates by consumers.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: Thus far, participating generation companies and retailers have been providing sufficient TRECS and retail contracts with significant fixed price components to meet demand, on a voluntary basis.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng) (for the Minister of Trade and Industry)
sentences.text: To ensure that electricity retailers do not impose unfair contractual terms on consumers under TRECS, EMA has worked directly with retailers to ensure that contractual terms such as prices and security deposit requirements are reasonably set.

sections.label: TRECS contract availability figures
sections.summary: 200 megawatts of TRECS contracts were available for February, and at least 300 megawatts remained as of 28 February 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Earlier on, I did share in this House that there were 200 megawatts of contracts available for TRECS for February.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: As of 28 February 2022, there were at least 300 megawatts of contracts that were still available.
